_comment_ProtectDescendantsOf: The entire live subtree under these is spared - a dev server still attached to a running editor or agent is in use, not garbage.
_comment_ReapWhenOrphaned: The one exception to Blacklist + ProtectDescendantsOf. claude.exe is one agent host per VS Code window, holding its MCP servers, node children and a conhost. Closing a chat does not end it - only closing the window does. If VS Code crashes instead of exiting cleanly, that whole tree becomes immortal. Reaped ONLY when the parent is dead, after OrphanGraceMinutes.
_comment_IdleAgents: Second exception: an agent host alive under a LIVE editor window but untouched. Sessions pile up one claude.exe each and only die with the window. Two triggers, both requiring IdleAgentHours of hourly samples (%LOCALAPPDATA%\proc-reaper\agent-activity.json): idle = own CPU grew <= IdleAgentCpuBudgetSec across the window (measured: abandoned drift 16-35 s/hour, used sessions land above 300 s/8h); stale = older than IdleAgentMaxAgeHours with no established non-loopback TCP connection (catches busy-loopers the CPU budget spares, without killing a hung-but-connected API stream). Killed with the whole MCP/LSP subtree, dev servers included - an 8h-untouched stand restarts in one command.
_comment_Whitelist: Only these names are ever considered in default (non-aggressive) mode. Name without .exe, case-insensitive.
_comment_Blacklist: Never touched, even in aggressive mode - as a target, as a duplicate, or as a descendant of something reaped. Device stacks belong here: killing an input/RGB helper re-enumerates its HID devices and freezes the mouse for seconds. Logitech G HUB (lghub*, logi_lamparray_service) is explicitly out of every rule - it is not cleaned and not restarted by us.
_comment_WindowExempt: Processes with a visible window are normally skipped; these are console helpers and get reaped anyway when orphaned.
_comment_DuplicateExempt: Excluded from the duplicate rule. conhost's command line is the generic 'conhost.exe 0x4' for every instance, so grouping by it would treat unrelated live consoles as copies.
_comment_TransientNames: Short-lived BY DESIGN. Reaped only when ALL hold: older than TransientMaxAgeMinutes, zero CPU across the sample, no children, no sockets, no window. NOT a general 'kill idle' rule - an idle language server is working, it is waiting.
_comment_ListenerMaxAgeHours: A process with a LISTENING TCP socket younger than this is immune from every rule - agent-started dev servers look orphaned by design (transient Claude shells) but are in use. Older listeners are leaked garbage and get reaped as usual. 0 disables the protection.
_comment_Protect: Extra names or literal PIDs that must never be reaped.
_comment_ProtectPorts: Ports of a local service kept up ON PURPOSE (for example the API and web ports of a self-hosted tool). The listening process, its whole subtree AND the chain that spawned it are immune with no age cap. ListenerMaxAgeHours is not enough for these two reasons: it covers the listener alone, so the pnpm/cmd/node --watch above it still died and left half a stand (2026-09-01: the API lost its --watch supervisor, vite lost its parent, and the panel read as 'switched itself off'), and it expires after 12 h, which is exactly when an always-on panel is still wanted.
_comment_ProtectCommandLineMatch: Regexes over the full command line; a match immunises that process and its subtree. For supervisors holding no port of their own - a keepalive watchdog of such a service would otherwise be an orphan like any other and get reaped exactly while the panel it guards is down.
